description: Source-lore pass 5 imports unsavory merchant guilds, criminal trade groups, slaver organizations, indentured servitude, slavery, oppressed life, and abolition/resistance material as source-backed wiki entries.

entries.title: Unsavory Trade in Kaysender
entries.summary: Beneath Kaysender's reputable trade fleets lies a shadow economy of rogue traders, exploitative guilds, smugglers, slavers, spies, counterfeiters, poachers, and brokers of forbidden knowledge.
body: Not all trade and commerce in Kaysender operates above board. Beneath the veneer of reputable merchant fleets lies a shadowy network of rogue traders, exploitative guilds, and slaver organizations that thrive in the chaos of the floating islands.

These groups prey on the vulnerabilities of a fractured world. Remote islands, weak governments, desperate settlements, drifting routes, corrupt elites, and draconic territories create opportunities for those willing to treat people, creatures, relics, secrets, and economies as commodities.

Major unsavory groups include [[black-chain-consortium|The Black Chain Consortium]], [[rusted-compass-company|The Rusted Compass Company]], [[crimson-fog-cartel|The Crimson Fog Cartel]], [[bonehold-syndicate|The Bonehold Syndicate]], [[broken-coin-guild|The Broken Coin Guild]], [[sable-tide|The Sable Tide]], [[chainwing-exchange|The Chainwing Exchange]], and [[tarnished-veil|The Tarnished Veil]].

This economy overlaps with [[indentured-servitude|indentured servitude]], [[slavery-in-kaysender|slavery]], [[black-fleet|piracy]], [[dragon-lords|Dragon Lord]] labor demands, black-market alchemy, forbidden magic, intelligence networks, and protected wealthy buyers who rely on distance and deniability.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Unsavory Merchant Guilds, Trade Groups, and Slaver Organizations in Kaysender

entries.title: The Black Chain Consortium
entries.summary: The Black Chain Consortium is a sprawling slaver network that traffics humanoids, rare magical creatures, and sentient constructs across the skies.
body: The Black Chain Consortium is a sprawling slaver network operating in secret across Kaysender's skies. It traffics humanoid captives, rare magical creatures, and sentient constructs, feeding markets that respectable society claims to despise while many powerful buyers quietly sustain them.

Its ships are dull gray and unmarked, designed to blend into misty skies. Some vessels are reinforced with iron cages and barred windows to hold living cargo. Its flagship, the Iron Maw, is a heavily armored prison ship capable of holding hundreds of captives in reinforced holds.

The Consortium targets remote islands and vulnerable settlements, raiding under cover of night and abducting entire populations. Slave auctions are held on secret floating platforms called Chain Havens, hidden within turbulent air currents or protected by powerful magic.
The Consortium is feared and despised by most people, but its customers include wealthy elites and certain [[dragon-lords|Dragon Lords]] seeking cheap labor, exotic pets, or living trophies.

entries.title: The Rusted Compass Company
entries.summary: The Rusted Compass Company is a group of underhanded scavenger-merchants who salvage wrecks, plunder ruins, smuggle illegal goods, and fly false flags.
body: The Rusted Compass Company is made up of underhanded merchants and scavengers who profit from salvaging wrecked airships, plundering ruins, and smuggling illegal goods.

Their ships are cobbled together from scavenged parts, with mismatched sails and patchwork hulls. Many display a rusted compass emblem, but they often fly false flags to disguise allegiance and operate in both lawful and lawless territory.

They scavenge battlefields and shipwrecks, often arriving suspiciously quickly after a conflict or storm. Their cargo includes banned magical artifacts, cursed relics, stolen goods, and other contraband.
The Company is tolerated where hard-to-find goods are needed and reviled where its disregard for law, ownership, and the dead is impossible to ignore.

entries.title: The Crimson Fog Cartel
entries.summary: The Crimson Fog Cartel smuggles addictive magical substances, alchemical poisons, illegal enchantments, black-market potions, and cursed powders through crimson-mist ships.
body: The Crimson Fog Cartel is a smuggling and drug-running operation dealing in addictive magical substances, alchemical poisons, illegal enchantments, black-market potions, cursed alchemical concoctions, and magical powders.

Its ships are sleek and fast, designed to evade pursuit. They use magical cloaks of crimson mist to obscure movement, giving the Cartel its name. Hidden compartments and enchanted holds conceal illicit cargo.

The Cartel operates from hidden bases in the Scarlet Veil, a fog-shrouded region of drifting islands. It supplies desperate or morally dubious buyers and enforces loyalty among clients and suppliers with ruthless violence.
The Cartel is infamous for ruining lives through addiction and for being one of the most dangerous organizations to cross in the shadow economy.

entries.title: The Bonehold Syndicate
entries.summary: The Bonehold Syndicate trades in necromantic goods, undead labor, cursed artifacts, enchanted bones, desecrated ruins, and forbidden magic.
body: The Bonehold Syndicate trades in necromantic goods and forbidden magics, including undead labor, cursed artifacts, and enchanted bones. It is one of the most openly macabre organizations in Kaysender's criminal economy.
Its ships are grim and ominous, with black sails stitched from hide and hulls adorned with skeletal motifs. Its flagship, The Wailing Gale, is said to carry a cursed crew of revenants and wraiths.
The Syndicate supplies undead workers for dangerous sky-mineral mines and other perilous labor. It harvests bones and artifacts from ancient ruins, often desecrating sacred sites in the process.
Most civilized societies shun the Syndicate, but necromancers, warlords, and desperate [[dragon-lords|Dragon Lords]] prize its goods.

entries.title: The Broken Coin Guild
entries.summary: The Broken Coin Guild is a network of counterfeiters, forgers, and deceptive traders that floods markets with fake goods, counterfeit currency, and fraudulent magical items.
body: The Broken Coin Guild is a guild of counterfeiters, forgers, and deceptive traders. It undermines economies by flooding markets with fake goods, counterfeit currency, forged documents, fraudulent magical items, and counterfeit potions.
Its ships are modest and unassuming, disguised as legitimate merchant vessels. Hidden workshops aboard those ships produce false goods and enchanted forgeries during travel.

The Guild sells fake magical items and counterfeit potions disguised as high-quality goods from reputable guilds. It also manipulates local economies, destabilizing regions so it can profit from the resulting chaos.
Merchants and adventurers alike revile the Broken Coin Guild because its goods are often indistinguishable from the real thing until it is too late.

entries.title: The Sable Tide
entries.summary: The Sable Tide is a shadow network of spies and assassins masquerading as a trade guild, specializing in espionage, sabotage, infiltration, and political murder.
body: The Sable Tide is a shadowy network of spies and assassins masquerading as a trade guild. Its services range from espionage to sabotage, often targeting rival merchant fleets, governments, and political figures.

Its ships are sleek, painted black, and stripped of visible markings. They often travel under the guise of independent traders. Stealth enchantments allow them to slip past patrols and infiltrate enemy ports.

The Sable Tide plants agents inside merchant fleets and governments to gather information or disrupt operations. It also smuggles assassins and spies into secure locations, neutralizing rivals for clients who prefer deniability.
Few know the organization's true extent. Its name is whispered in fear, and its involvement in disasters is often suspected but rarely proven.

entries.title: The Chainwing Exchange
entries.summary: The Chainwing Exchange is the black-market counterpart to the Aetherbound Company, trafficking illegal creatures, endangered skybeasts, intelligent species, and biological weapons.
body: The Chainwing Exchange trades in rare and often illegal creatures, including endangered skybeasts and intelligent species. It is the black-market counterpart to [[aetherbound-company|the Aetherbound Company]].

Its ships are reinforced for dangerous cargo, with massive containment pods suspended beneath their hulls. Its largest ship, the Iron Feather, is a flying fortress capable of housing entire herds of captured skybeasts.

The Exchange captures creatures through illegal hunts, poaching from protected reserves, or cruel breeding programs. Auctions in remote locations attract buyers seeking exotic pets, mounts, prestige creatures, or biological weapons.
The Exchange is detested by conservationists and [[sheffels|skybeast]] shepherds for driving species toward extinction, but its goods remain sought after by the wealthy and powerful.

entries.title: The Tarnished Veil
entries.summary: The Tarnished Veil is a shadow network of merchants dealing in secrets, blackmail, forbidden knowledge, classified maps, political leverage, and delicate criminal mediation.
body: The Tarnished Veil is a shadowy network of merchants dealing in secrets, blackmail, and forbidden knowledge. It acts as the ultimate broker of information in the darker corners of Kaysender's trade world.
Its ships are nondescript and regularly change appearance using illusory magic. Its mobile headquarters, the Ebon Whisper, constantly relocates to avoid discovery.

The Veil trades in political secrets, blackmail material, classified maps, forbidden documents, and sensitive information. It often collaborates with other unsavory groups, acting as an intermediary for delicate negotiations.
It is feared and mistrusted because no one is safe from its prying eyes. A secret in the hands of the Tarnished Veil is not information; it is leverage waiting for the right buyer.

entries.title: Indentured Servitude in Kaysender
entries.summary: Indentured servitude in Kaysender is often called a lesser evil, but it commonly functions as debt bondage enforced by contracts, magical seals, inherited debt, and elite labor demand.
body: Indentured servitude in Kaysender is often portrayed as a lesser evil compared to slavery, but in truth it is often a thinly veiled form of bondage. Economic disparity, political unrest, and the unregulated wilds of the floating islands allow exploitation to persist under respectable legal language.

Many people fall into servitude through debt contracts after taking loans they cannot repay. These contracts are bought and sold like commodities, binding debtors to years or even a lifetime of unpaid labor.

Servants are forced into grueling work: hazardous sky-mineral mines, merchant fleets, skybeast ranches, alchemical works, and dangerous outer-island infrastructure. Contracts may be magically sealed, and fleeing can bring severe punishment.
In some cases, debt becomes generational. Children born into these arrangements are treated as the property of creditors until they can buy freedom, which is nearly impossible for most families.

Unsavory merchant guilds justify servitude as necessary for economic survival. Wealthy [[dragon-lords|Dragon Lords]] and minor sky rulers enforce such systems to keep labor flowing into mines, fleets, ranches, refineries, and armies.

entries.title: Slavery in Kaysender
entries.summary: Slavery in Kaysender is a brutal institution operating in shadows and openly in lawless territories, fed by raids, auctions, camps, criminal fleets, wealthy buyers, and weak enforcement.
body: Slavery in Kaysender is a stark and brutal institution, operating both in shadow and openly in lawless territories or under despotic rulers. It persists because the powerful profit from it and because enforcement is weak where islands drift beyond reliable authority.

Sky pirates, including crews loosely affiliated with the [[black-fleet|Black Fleet]], raid villages and isolated islands to capture people. Captives are sold to slavers or directly to wealthy buyers. Secret floating platforms serve as slave auction houses, where humanoid captives, rare magical creatures, and sentient constructs are sold to the highest bidder.

Many enslaved people are sent to the worst places in the world: quarries on jagged floating rocks, toxic alchemical refineries, mines plagued by instability, and regions crawling with skybeasts. Conditions are brutal, punishments public, and autonomy deliberately destroyed.

Humanoids of many peoples are at risk, including dwarves, elves, humans, and even dragonkin, especially in border regions where law enforcement is weak. Intelligent magical creatures are captured, broken, and sold as tools of war or status symbols. Sentient golems and constructs may be magically bound and treated as objects despite awareness.

The practice is an open secret among some [[dragon-lords|Dragon Lords]], many of whom rely on forced labor to support armies, luxuries, and massive hoards. Other islands outlaw slavery, but clandestine operations continue wherever profit exceeds fear of punishment.

sections.heading: Life of the Oppressed
body: Those trapped in these systems live under relentless toil, constant fear, cramped housing, disease, public punishment, and lack of autonomy. Magical collars, brands, or tattoos may be used to control captives through pain or paralysis.

Resistance persists through whispered rumors, escape plans, rare uprisings, and the work of groups such as [[free-sky-brotherhood|the Free Sky Brotherhood]], which smuggles the oppressed toward safe havens.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Slavery: The Darkest Chain / Life of the Oppressed

entries.title: Abolition and Sanctuary Movements
entries.summary: Reformist islands, resistance movements, adventurers, mercenaries, and secret groups fight Kaysender's systems of servitude and slavery despite fierce opposition from those who profit.
body: Not everyone in Kaysender accepts the systems of servitude and slavery. Certain sky islands, especially those aligned with reformist factions, have declared themselves sanctuaries for escaped slaves and outlawed indentured servitude.

Resistance movements are growing. Some adventurers and mercenaries dedicate their lives to disrupting slaver networks, freeing captives, exposing auctions, sabotaging prison ships, and escorting fugitives to safe havens.

The [[free-sky-brotherhood|Free Sky Brotherhood]] is remembered in whispered tales as one such force, smuggling the oppressed away from bondage and toward sanctuary. These stories give hope even when uprisings are crushed and conditions become harsher afterward.

The fight for abolition is met with fierce opposition because exploitation is deeply entrenched. Those who profit from debt bondage, slavery, creature trafficking, and forced labor will fight to preserve their power with ships, magic, legal excuses, mercenaries, and terror.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Resistance and Hope / Cultural Divide and the Fight for Abolition
